function.name: protein_info_get_sequence_and_3D
function.description: Retrive the sequence and 3D models of proteins. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

model_3d.description: Set true to get 3D model of the protein.

message.reasoning: The user wants to retrieve protein sequences and 3D models for human HbA1c, normal hemoglobin, and rat hemoglobin. They want the sequences and 3D models. We have a function to retrieve sequence and 3D models. We need to call the function for each protein. The function expects protein_name string and optional model_3d boolean. We should call it for each protein. The user didn't specify whether they want all three in one call or separate calls. The function likely returns data for one protein at a time. So we need to call it three times. We can do that. We'll call the function for "Human HbA1c", "Normal Hemoglobin" (maybe "Human Hemoglobin"?), and "Rat Hemoglobin". But we need to be careful: "normal hemoglobin" might refer to human hemoglobin? Or maybe "HbA"? The user says "正常血紅蛋白" which is normal hemoglobin. That could be human hemoglobin A (HbA). So we need to get sequence and 3D model for human HbA1c, human HbA, and rat hemoglobin. Let's call the function with those names. We'll set model_3d to true (default). We'll produce three calls. Then we will output the results. The function returns any. We'll just call it.
